newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes barely changed, sluggish.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes barely changed, sluggish.

text.p: Precious metals markets again focused on the platinum group metals (PGMs) on Tuesday after gold and silver settled into narrow, undecided ranges, dealers said.
"Gold is stuck between those who want it to go higher and those who want it to go lower, so the dealers are just thrashing around," one dealer said.
The stronger dollar was a background factor for gold.
But the balance of comment from the German government and the Bundesbank on revaluing gold reserves was bringing a few cent moves either way, the dealer added.
Most conspicuous was the way prices oscillated on a magazine article that Bonn planned to sell gold and on the government's swift denial of the report.
Gold was fixed at $343.80 per ounce, just 10 cents lower than Monday afternoon.
The dollar was pushing against 1.73 marks on its shared safe-haven status against continuing uncertainty about the start-up time and robustness of European Monetary Union.
A 1999 start up was under a shadow due to the view that Germany's plan to revalue gold reserves to help clear old debts was a fudge of entry requirements.
The perception that the new French socialist government would be less given to austerity also raised questions about a 1999 start.
Gold was facing resistance above $344.00, dealers said.
The weaker Australian dollar meant the gold price was around A$352, normally well above local producers' forward selling threshold.
"They have not been selling as the low interest rates there mean they are not getting the contango they want," a dealer said, adding that a dollar or two more might be tempting.
If gold can break $344.50 and get through $347, it could be "off to the races," the dealer added.
The PGMs were steady in Europe after a volatile night in which stop-losses on Nymex and short covering on Tocom had sent palladium in particular through several figures.
It was quoted at $178.00/$182.00, up $7.50, as the market watched for developments between the Russian export negotiators and Japanese importers in Tokyo.
Russia, the largest export of the metal, has been off the market since last December due to administrative issues.
Silver was unchanged at $4.74/$4.76 but forward rates were tighter. --Brian Spoors +44 171 542 8058
